I'm checking EV-06 against the criteria: the title is empty, which isn't a criterion, so that's fine. QUS-001 looks met, since the role, action, and benefit are all present, and QUS-002 and QUS-003 also hold. For QUS-004 I'm weighing whether the benefit "build user experiences based on more than one dataset more easily" reads as a justification rather than a benefit.

I'm now checking QUS-005 and QUS-006: "more easily" is vague with no measure, and "use metadata to get results" doesn't say what kind of results or operation is meant, so I'm flagging QUS-006 as a defect. For QUS-008, I'm comparing EV-06 with CTX-OS-065, which has the same role, action, and benefit, differing only in "metadata" versus "data", so it looks like a likely duplicate that I'd mark as blocking.

I'm going through the remaining invariant checks: the story looks independent, since no dependencies are named, and it's valuable because the benefit is stated outright. INV-003 fails because the scope is unclear, with no defined metadata, results, datasets or format, so it can't be estimated yet. I'm leaning toward INV-004 being met, though it's hard to judge without the scope.

I'm checking DOR-001 next: the story needs data from existing datasets, and the integration with them isn't stated, so I'm leaning toward marking it as not met. I'll also call the reference-story search to help estimate the size, since the scope is still unclear.

I'm checking whether the datasets' metadata dependency is explicit, and I'll count it as a defect since the dependency is evident but unstated. I'm also looking at whether the story defines any limits, validation, or error cases for querying multiple datasets, such as incompatible schemas, and I'm treating their absence as a major defect. Next I'm checking the non-functional requirements for this multi-dataset API.

Defects so far are QUS-006, QUS-008, INV-003, INV-005, DOR-001 and DOR-002, so the call is to return the story rather than accept it. Before deciding, I want a size estimate, so I'll look up reference stories.

recomendaciones.texto: Posible duplicado: CTX-OS-065 pide lo mismo para el mismo rol (API User), acción (obtener resultados de múltiples datasets) y beneficio, cambiando solo 'metadata' por 'data'. Confirmar con producto si son la misma HU y fusionarlas, o explicar qué aporta 'metadata' que la diferencia de CTX-OS-065.

Agregar criterios de aceptación verificables, por ejemplo: con un conjunto de datasets indicado, la consulta devuelve resultados de todos ellos; con un dataset inexistente, se muestra un error. Cada criterio debe tener un resultado observable.

Definir el alcance para estimar: qué metadatos se usan, qué tipo de resultados se obtienen (búsqueda, filtro, agregación, unión), cuántos datasets se admiten por consulta y qué formato de respuesta se espera.

Reemplazar términos vagos: 'more easily' no tiene medida ni criterio que lo concrete, y 'get results' no indica qué resultados. Describir el beneficio en términos observables y precisar qué significa obtener resultados de múltiples datasets.

Definir las reglas y casos de error relevantes: qué pasa si los datasets tienen esquemas o metadatos incompatibles, si un dataset no existe o no es accesible, y si hay límite de datasets o de resultados por consulta.
Nombrar la dependencia de la que salen los metadatos de los datasets (por ejemplo, el servicio o almacén de metadatos del proyecto) y confirmar que está disponible para esta HU.
